title: The first balloon riders were a sheep, duck and rooster!
question: Did you know the first passengers in a hot-air balloon were a sheep, a duck and a rooster?
answer: The first passengers to fly in a hot-air balloon, in France in 1783, were a sheep, a duck and a rooster.

visual.what: A big colourful balloon floats in a blue sky. In its basket a fluffy sheep, a duck and a rooster look out happily. Big question mark in the sky.

parts.text: Did you know the first passengers in a hot-air balloon were a sheep, a duck and a rooster?

visual.what: Two old-fashioned French brothers in 1700s clothes stand beside a giant sky-blue balloon on the ground. A small sign reads France, 1783.

parts.text: In 1783, two brothers in France built a giant balloon.

visual.what: Cross-section of a balloon. Cold air dots packed close outside, hot air dots spread out inside. Red arrows point up from the balloon.

parts.text: But how does a balloon float?
Hot air is lighter than cold air, so it rises.

visual.what: A king and queen in fancy clothes watch from a crowd as the balloon lifts. The sheep, duck and rooster stand in a wicker basket. Calendar shows 19 September.

parts.text: On 19 September, a king and queen watched. The sheep, the duck and the rooster rode in a basket.

visual.what: A balloon flight path drawn as a line over football pitches, about four and a half pitches long. Label says about 480 metres.

parts.text: They flew about 480 metres. That is more than four football pitches.

visual.what: A balloon tied to the ground by a rope with a person in the basket, then a free balloon floating away. Calendar pages flip.

parts.text: Weeks later, people flew too. But the animals went first!

visual.what: Huy and Mai wave at the camera with the three animals peeking out of a small balloon basket behind them. Follow button pops up.

parts.text: Follow Ask Huy for more surprising facts!

facts.claim: The first passenger flight in a hot air balloon was on 19 September 1783 and carried a sheep, a duck and a rooster.
The balloon was built by the Montgolfier brothers and shown to King Louis XVI and Queen Marie Antoinette. The flight went about 480 metres.
The Montgolfier brothers were from Annonay, France.
Hot air is lighter than the same amount of cold air, so it rises and lifts the balloon.
The first flight carrying a person was on 15 October 1783 with the balloon tied to the ground. The first free flight was on 21 November 1783.

description: Before any person flew free in a balloon, a sheep, a duck and a rooster took the first ride in France in 1783. Find out how it floated and who watched!
